services.intro: Our licensed plumbers work on homes across Niles, from its older post-war neighborhoods to newer builds near the Golf Mill area.

cards.paragraph: [A September 2008 storm dropped about 9.5 inches of rain on Niles in 15 hours, damaging roughly 781 homes and overwhelming the village’s combined sewer system](https://www.icma.org/sites/default/files/308569_Niles-Stormwater%20Relief-UPDATED.doc), with records showing the same areas had flooded repeatedly since the 1970s. A storm that size is rare, but any heavy rain still tests an aging combined line. For a homeowner, that means a backup can show up with little warning. We camera-inspect your line, clear what’s blocking it, and talk through backflow protection.

Niles has a documented history of flooding tied to its combined sewers, and the village has spent years mapping and patching a system that wasn’t built for today’s storms. When heavy rain hits, it doesn’t check the clock, and a backed-up line can send water into your home at any hour. Waiting only makes the cleanup bigger. Call any time, including weekends and holidays - our phone line never closes, and we’ll get a plumber to you as soon as we can.

[Most Niles homes date to the postwar boom, with 60.3% built between 1940 and 1969 and a median year built of 1965](https://cmap.illinois.gov/wp-content/uploads/dlm_uploads/Niles.pdf), so a lot of houses still run on original clay or cast iron drain lines. Cast iron scales up inside over the decades, and clay joints let tree roots work in, so a quick clear rarely lasts. That usually shows up as the same kitchen or basement drain backing up again. We clear the line and run a camera through it.

[Niles shares the Morton Grove/Niles Water Commission, which buys Lake Michigan water from Evanston instead of Chicago](https://mortongroveil.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/2025-CCR-ANNUAL-REPORT_FINAL_PUBLISH.pdf), a setup both villages built to move away from Chicago’s rising rates. It’s still treated lake water, so the usual minerals still settle inside a tank over the years. A heater installed years ago has likely run through more than one source by now. If yours rumbles or runs out of hot water early, that’s worth a look.

Fixtures in Niles’ older homes have usually been swapped out at least once, but the shutoff valves and seals behind them don’t always get replaced at the same time. That mismatch is often why a toilet runs constantly or a shower valve starts leaking behind the tile years after a remodel. Left alone, a running toilet adds up on the water bill, and a hidden leak can damage the subfloor. We fix what can be fixed, replace what can’t, and install new fixtures and valves when you’re ready.

Many Niles homes still carry original supply lines behind plaster walls, and decades-old pipe corrodes from the inside where you can’t see it. A slow leak can run for weeks before a stain or soft spot in the floor gives it away, and by then it may have reached the framing underneath. If you notice a drop in water pressure or a damp spot that won’t dry, it’s worth tracing down. We find the leak, repair or replace the pipe, and check nearby sections.

cards.paragraph: Given [Niles’ history of combined sewer overwhelm during heavy storms](https://www.icma.org/sites/default/files/308569_Niles-Stormwater%20Relief-UPDATED.doc), a working sump pump is often the last line of defense for a basement. A pump that’s aging, too small for the job, or running without battery backup is most likely to quit during a power outage - right when you need it most. A failed pump usually means standing water within hours. We test, repair and replace sump pumps, and can add a battery backup for when the power drops.

faq.q: Do you have plumbers near me in Niles?
faq.a: Yes. Our plumbers work all over Niles and the nearby north suburban towns, including Morton Grove, Lincolnwood and Skokie. Call us 24/7 and we’ll get a plumber to you.

faq.q: Are you licensed and bonded in Illinois?
faq.a: Yes. We’re licensed and bonded in Illinois, and we’ve been serving Chicagoland homeowners since 1993.

faq.q: How much does a plumber cost in Niles?
faq.a: It depends on the job. The main factors are what’s wrong, how hard it is to reach, the parts or materials needed and the age of your plumbing. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins, so you know the cost going in.

Storms that size are rare, but a hard rain can still strain an older line.

faq.q: Why do I keep getting the same drain clog?
faq.a: [Most Niles homes were built in the postwar years, with a median year built of 1965](https://cmap.illinois.gov/wp-content/uploads/dlm_uploads/Niles.pdf), and many still run on original clay or cast iron drain lines. Roots or scale inside them cause the same spot to clog again and again. We run a camera through the line so you know whether the pipe itself needs repair.

faq.q: Does Niles get its water from Chicago?
faq.a: Not entirely. [Niles shares the Morton Grove/Niles Water Commission, which buys Lake Michigan water from Evanston](https://mortongroveil.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/2025-CCR-ANNUAL-REPORT_FINAL_PUBLISH.pdf) rather than the City of Chicago. It’s still treated lake water, so the usual mineral buildup inside a water heater still applies over time.
